items.title: Agent Registry release notes: standalone skill governance
items.rationale: Immutable skill revisions, verified publishers, policy bindings, and semantic discovery make this a durable Agent control-plane update. Existing Agent Registry coverage makes a focused refresh more appropriate than a duplicate launch post.

history.note: Verified the July 23 Preview release in Google Cloud documentation and shortlisted it as a refresh or governance follow-up.

items.title: How to manage AI investments in the agentic era
items.rationale: The cost-per-accepted-outcome framing is durable and operationally useful, but the model-efficiency numbers are first-party claims and the topic overlaps existing GPT-5.6 and governance coverage.

history.note: Verified the primary article and retained it for an outcome-economics angle rather than a model launch summary.

items.title: EU AI Act enforcement: agent transparency becomes an engineering requirement
items.rationale: The Commission's primary announcement confirms that enforcement and new transparency requirements began on 2026-08-02; the implementation guidance names concrete disclosure and machine-readable marking obligations. This is a durable governance-to-runtime-controls angle and a refresh/follow-up to existing governance and agent-security coverage, not a duplicate launch summary. Legal scope and product-specific applicability remain items for human review.

history.note: Verified the European Commission's 2026-07-31 announcement and the AI Act Service Desk agent FAQ during the 7-day backfill; flagged a governance/security refresh angle effective 2026-08-02.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic: maintenance mode and AgentCore migration
items.rationale: AWS documentation states that Bedrock Agents is now Agents Classic, entered maintenance mode, stopped accepting new customers on 2026-07-30, and recommends AgentCore as the migration path. The page includes a capability matrix, account allowlist behavior, model-freeze implications, and migration procedure. This is a durable platform migration and governance refresh for existing AgentCore and Enterprise RAG coverage; account-specific migration scope and cost still require human verification.

history.note: Seven-day backfill found the AWS maintenance-mode guide and verified the 2026-07-30 effective date, AgentCore recommendation, unchanged Knowledge Bases/Guardrails, and documented capability gaps.

items.title: TREC RAG 2026: an agent-first evaluation track
items.rationale: The official TREC RAG 2026 track defines separate retrieval and grounded-answer tasks, an agent-first workflow, a new ClimbMix-400b corpus, and the RAGDoll evaluation toolkit. The site repository was updated on 2026-08-08 before the submission deadline. This is durable evaluation infrastructure rather than a product announcement; results, manual judgments, corpus licensing, and production validity remain unknown.

history.note: Verified the official TREC RAG 2026 homepage, 2026-08-08 site-repository updates, agent-first retrieval/RAG task split, RAGDoll toolkit, ClimbMix-400b corpus, and 2026-08-08 submission deadline. Collected as durable evaluation infrastructure with results and judgment quality left unknown.

items.title: GitHub Copilot enterprise MCP allowlists and agent activity telemetry
items.rationale: GitHub's official release and managed-settings reference make MCP governance concrete: allow and deny lists, fail-closed behavior, multi-layer intersection, URL canonicalization, and client support. The adjacent usage-metrics update exposes per-agent activity for rollout and licensing review. This is a durable policy-and-observability angle that extends existing agent security/governance routes; independent bypass efficacy and adoption results remain unknown.

history.note: Seven-day backfill verified the 2026-08-06 MCP allowlist release, enterprise schema and deployment docs, plus the 2026-08-07 per-agent usage metrics API. Preserved the boundary that serverName is not a security control and first-party Copilot servers are exempt from deny rules.

items.title: Claude Managed Agents: budgets, advisors, locality, skills, and inference hooks
items.rationale: Anthropic's official release notes and Managed Agents docs add hard public-list-price session budgets, advisor-based multi-agent escalation, inference geography, repository skills, and enterprise inference hooks with signed allow/deny decisions. These features make cost, delegation, locality, provenance, and policy interception runtime state. The candidate is a governance/platform follow-up to existing Anthropic memory and enterprise control-plane coverage; beta availability, independent enforcement, and deployment cost remain unknown.

history.note: Seven-day backfill verified Anthropic release-note entries dated 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-05 plus the budget, multi-agent orchestration, GitHub, and inference-hook references. Preserved the documented one-request budget overshoot, shared multi-agent cap, beta headers, and unknown independent enforcement evidence.

items.title: Open Secure AI Alliance: open tools for securing AI agents
items.rationale: NVIDIA's primary announcement describes the Open Secure AI Alliance as a cross-industry effort to build and share open security tooling for the full agent stack, including identity, harnesses, guardrails, logs, and evaluation. It also names concrete contributions such as NOOA, SPIFFE/SPIRE, Safetensors, Lightwell, and MDASH. The source is first-party advocacy and does not establish adoption, incident-reduction outcomes, or neutral governance, but the stack-level framing is durable and complements existing agent governance coverage.

history.note: Daily scan found no newer qualifying primary announcement in the 72-hour window. After extending the technical/governance search to 30 days, verified NVIDIA's July 27 announcement and the Linux Foundation's matching July 27 post, including the NOOA contribution and full-stack agent security framing. Keep as a durable candidate; SAFE incident-reporting details remain secondary and unverified by a primary RFC in this run.

items.title: Agent Plugins 1.0: one portable package for skills and MCP servers
items.rationale: GitHub documents Agent Plugins 1.0 as an open package format that bundles skills and MCP server configuration for portable installation across VS Code, Copilot CLI, the Copilot SDK, and the Copilot app. The specification, example repository, and enterprise managed-settings/MCP allowlist controls make this a concrete packaging-and-governance surface rather than a feature teaser. The cross-client standard is durable, while adoption and security efficacy remain unmeasured.

history.note: Verified the 2026-08-12 GitHub Changelog release, the agent-plugins.org author guide, the published 1.0 specification, the example plugin repository, and GitHub's managed-settings/MCP allowlist framing. No duplicate canonical URL was present in the Blog Radar ledger. Kept the open-standard and policy-boundary claims separate from any unmeasured security or adoption outcome.

items.title: Amazon Quick agentic AI capabilities enter AWS GovCloud (US-West)
items.rationale: AWS's official announcement adds Amazon Quick's custom chat agents, mission-specific workflows, least-privilege Spaces, GCC High connectors, and in-region inference to GovCloud (US-West) under a FedRAMP Class D environment. This is a useful enterprise deployment pattern for regulated agentic AI, although it is a first-party availability announcement with no independent efficacy or adoption evidence and a narrower audience than the general governance series.

history.note: Verified AWS's 2026-08-11 primary announcement and its claims about GovCloud (US-West), FedRAMP Class D, custom agents, least-privilege Spaces, GCC High connectors, and regional inference. No duplicate canonical URL was present. Treat compliance availability as a documented product boundary, not proof of agent safety or mission outcomes.
